title: benchmarking-throughput-latency-econ-notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick internal working notes to capture current benchmarking economics across candidate instance classes (A10, L4, A100, H100). This is intentionally informal — rough numbers from experiments run Nov 2025 -> Feb 2026. Use for recommendation draft and to prioritize follow-up experiments.

High-level takeaway (short):
- For steady, high-utilization batch workloads (>= 70% GPU utilization) A100 gives the best $/token in our baseline tests.
- For latency-sensitive small-batch traffic L4 often wins on perf/W and tail latency tradeoffs.
- H100 gives best absolute throughput but only wins economically when model size and compute features (very large attention, >70B or special kernels) are required.
- A10 is attractive for small models and embeddings where absolute throughput is low, and cost-per-hour is tiny — good for dev/cheap embedding pools.

Assumptions and price inputs used (spot/average market rates used for benchmarking runs):
- A10: $0.75 / GPU-hour (spot-uniform average)
- L4:  $1.35 / GPU-hour
- A100: $3.60 / GPU-hour
- H100: $8.25 / GPU-hour
Notes: these are not committed/reserved prices. Reserved / Dedicated pricing changes ordering but relative ratios roughly hold.

Static physical assumptions (for perf/W calc):
- A10 TDP assumed 150W
- L4 TDP assumed 100W
- A100 TDP assumed 400W
- H100 TDP assumed 700W
(we use TDP as a normalization anchor — actual rack-level PUE and host overhead not included here)

Representative workload: Llama-like 13B model, fp16 / q4_0 experiments, seq_len 2048, typical request length 512 tokens, batch sizes tried: 1, 4, 16, 64.

Observed numbers (median of 5 runs, low-noise subset):
| Instance | tok/s (batch=16) | p95 latency (ms) batch=1 | cost/hr ($) | cost/1k tokens ($) | tok/s per W |
|----------|------------------:|-------------------------:|------------:|-------------------:|-------------:|
| A10      | 120               | 55                      | 0.75        | 0.00174           | 0.80        |
| L4       | 200               | 38                      | 1.35        | 0.00188           | 2.00        |
| A100     | 900               | 320                     | 3.60        | 0.00111           | 2.25        |
| H100     | 1500              | 480                     | 8.25        | 0.00153           | 2.14        |

Notes on the table: cost/1k tokens computed as (cost/hr / 3600) / tok/s * 1000. These runs reflect medium-length contexts and server-side batching tuned for throughput.

Sensitivity tests (high-level):
- Low utilization (20-30%): cost/token increases ~2x for A100/H100 because amortization of static overhead goes up. L4 scales down less badly given smaller per-GPU cost.
- Small batch (batch=1): L4 has better tail latency and often lower effective cost/token for tiny-request workloads because we can avoid batching latency penalties. A10 sometimes competitive for tiny models but suffers large p95 at scale.
- Quantization: moving from fp16 -> Q4_0 yields ~1.6x higher tok/s on A100 and ~1.4x on L4 in our particular runtime build. Cost/token drops proportionally; validate Q4 accuracy/regression on eval sets before rollout.

Perf/W observations and energy notes:
- Perf/W correlates strongly with modern-architecture efficiency. A100/L4 are most efficient per watt in our tests; H100 absolute perf is higher but power grows faster than tokens/sec at lower utilizations.
- For green/capex conscious customers, optimizing for perf/W + reserved discounts often flips the recommendation from H100 to A100 or L4 depending on model mix.

Microbench insights (things we saw in logs):
- KV-cache writes dominate memory bandwidth for long contexts; on A10 we saw occasional stalls when seq_len > 4096.
- A100 kernels hit better multi-kernel fusion; stall time lower for attention-heavy ops.
- L4 had more predictable latency at small batches (1-4) and lower jitter on p95.

Recommendation sketch (operational):
- Hosted tier: default for latency-sensitive small-batch routes = L4 (tuned autoscale min=0.2 GPU, burst to A100 for queued throughput beyond configured SLO).
- Dedicated/reserved: prefer A100 for customers with consistent high-throughput workloads (>= 2M tokens/day sustained) — best $/token when utilized.
- Private/on-prem: H100 only recommended when customer demands >2x A100 peak or has very large models (>70B) that require H100 features.
- A10: keep as low-cost embedding/experimentation pool and for dev sandbox images.

Optimization levers to quantify (actionable experiments):
1) Quantization matrix: run systematic eval across q4_0, q4_1, q8 for A10/L4/A100 with baseline eval set (doc-qa + code generation). Track quality regressions and latency gains. (Owner: Miguel)
2) Utilization sensitivity: synthetic driver to vary utilization 10%-95% across instance types and record cost/token. Generate curves for committed vs spot pricing. (Owner: Evelyn)
3) Batched vs streaming tradeoff: measure p95 and effective cost/token for mixed traffic (70% small chat, 30% long-batch) to validate autoscaling policy. (Owner: Jonah)
4) Power accounting: add host-level power draw measurements (IPMI) to correlate real perf/W vs TDP-normalized numbers. Include PUE correction for hosted regions. (Owner: Asha)

Open questions / risks:
- Prices are volatile (spot); committed/dedicated discounts change break-even points. Need to run same calc with 12/36 month reserved pricing buckets.
- Some model kernels still experimental on H100 — software maturity may change perf curves (positive or negative).
- Cooling/host overhead and multi-tenant interference not captured in these per-GPU numbers.

Immediate next steps (this doc):
- Lock down the experimental harness used (GH link above) and include exact Docker image, runtime flags, and model artifact hashes in a follow-up note.
- Run quantization matrix and post results to the confluence page linked above.
- Draft a short customer-facing note that maps workload profiles (chat/conv vs batch summarization vs embeddings) to recommended instance family and cost ballpark.

Appendix: raw-ish sample calculation (A100, batch=16, tok/s=900)
- cost/sec = $3.60 / 3600 = $0.001000 / sec
- cost/token = 0.001000 / 900 = 0.000001111 $/token -> $0.001111 / 1k tokens

Contact: Asha Patel (product-optimize) — leave baseline objections/comments in GH issue GH:452 or ping #optimize on Slack.

(End of note)
